title: Quotes: the basics
summary: Understand the Quotes list, quote numbers, statuses and how a quote flows from draft to accepted.

body.text: The **Quotes** page is where you build, price and send every customer proposal. Each quote gets a sequential number shown as **Q-1234**, and the list shows only the current version of each quote (older revisions are kept in version history).
Reading the list

For every quote you see the customer, the linked lead (if any), the total (including VAT), the status, the valid-until date, and who created it. Click a **Q-number** to open the quote in the editor; click the customer or lead to jump to their record.
Quote statuses

rows: Marked as sent to the customer. Frozen — revise to change it.
Customer accepted. A linked lead is marked won automatically.
Customer declined. You can revise it.

body.text: A quote can also be **superseded** (replaced by a revision) or **signed** (accepted online). Both states are permanently read-only.
Starting a new quote

items: Click **New quote** at the top of the Quotes page.
Pick the customer, and optionally link an open lead.
Add line items and any fees, then save.

body.text: You can also start a quote straight from a lead — it pre-fills the lead's product as the first line.
Deleting a quote
Use **Delete** to move a quote to the Trash. It is restorable for **60 days**. Deleting an accepted quote may reopen its lead if no other accepted quote remains.

title: Building and pricing a quote
summary: Add product and custom lines, apply discounts, add fees and delivery, set a deposit and choose the VAT basis.

body.text: The quote editor opens in a dialog with four tabs — **Build**, **Preview**, **Versions** and **Send**. The Build tab is where you assemble the quote; the running total updates live in the right-hand panel.
Adding line items
You can add two kinds of lines:

items: **Product line** — pick a catalogue product. Its name and base price fill in automatically, and if the product has colours you can set a **colour preference**.
**Custom line** — type your own description and price for anything not in the catalogue.

body.text: Each line has a **quantity**, a **unit price (R)** and an optional **discount %** (0–100). The line total is the discounted amount.
A colour preference can only be set on a catalogue product line, and it must be a colour configured for that product.
Fees and delivery

items: Add a **Delivery** or **Fee** line.
Give it a label (for example, 'Delivery to Cape Town').
Enter the amount. VAT is applied at 15%.

body.text: Deposit, VAT basis and settings
In the **Quote settings** panel you can set:

items: **Valid until** — the quote's expiry date.
**Pricing basis** — *Prices include VAT* (the default) or *Add VAT on top*.
**Deposit** — none, a percentage of the total, or a fixed rand amount. The total, deposit and balance-on-delivery are all shown.
**Terms** — the terms text printed on the quote.

body.text: Use the **Preview** tab to see exactly how the proposal will look to the customer before sending.

title: Sending, accepting and revising quotes
summary: Mark a quote sent, record acceptance or decline, and revise a customer-facing quote without overwriting it.

body.text: Once a quote leaves draft it becomes a fixed record — the customer must never see a quote change under them. To make changes to a sent or declined quote you create a **revision** instead.
Marking a quote sent

From the editor's **Send** tab choose **Save & mark sent**, or use **Mark sent** on the full quote record. This freezes the version at the exact price the customer received. A quote needs at least one line before it can be marked sent.
Recording the outcome

On a sent quote's record you can mark it **Accepted** or **Declined**. Accepting a quote that is linked to a lead automatically marks the lead **won**, triggers any lead automations, and flags a referral fee as earned if the deal came through a referral. Use **Back to draft** to reopen an accepted or declined quote.
If you move a quote out of 'accepted' and the lead has no other accepted quote, the lead is reopened so it no longer counts as a sale.
Creating a revision

items: Open the sent or declined quote's full record.
Click **↻ Create revision**. The quote is copied into a fresh editable draft with a new Q-number.
The original is marked superseded and kept read-only for the record.

body.text: A quote is locked from editing when a signing link is active, once it is signed, once it is superseded, or as soon as it leaves draft. Revoke the signing link or create a revision to make changes.
Version history and change requests

Every version stays on record. When a quote family has more than one version, a **Version history** panel lists them all. If a customer requests changes online, a banner appears on the quote with their note and a shortcut to create a revision.

title: Quote documents, printing and handover
summary: Print or PDF a quote, generate the invoice and sales agreement, and track fulfilment on an accepted quote.

body.text: The full quote record carries the print and document actions plus the fulfilment tracking that starts once a quote is accepted.
Printing and documents

items: **Print / PDF** — available on any quote.
**Invoice** and **Sales agreement** — appear once the quote is accepted.
**Generate** — owners can generate a builder-template document for the quote and file it in the repository.

body.text: Fulfilment tracker

An accepted quote shows a **Fulfilment** strip of badges: *Invoiced*, *Deposit paid*, *Delivery scheduled* and *Delivered*. Each lights up green as that step is completed. A shortcut links through to the Deliveries board to manage the handover.
Delivery photos

items: Open the accepted quote.
In the **Delivery photos** card, choose one or more images (your phone camera works).
Click **Upload**. Photos are filed on both the customer and the quote.

body.text: Line totals, quote totals and every printed document all use the same pricing rules, so a discount you set is reflected identically everywhere.

title: Managing deliveries and handovers
summary: Move accepted quotes through invoicing, deposit, scheduling and handover on the Deliveries board.

body.text: The **Deliveries** board tracks every accepted vehicle from sale to handover. A quote appears here the moment it is accepted and drops off once you mark it delivered. The board has four columns and a quote sits in whichever stage it has not yet completed.

rows: Signed/accepted — send and upload the invoice.
Upload proof of payment when it lands.

body.text: Working a card

items: In **To invoice**, attach the invoice file and click **Mark invoiced**.
In **Awaiting deposit**, attach the proof of payment and click **Deposit paid**.
In **Schedule delivery**, pick the date (and optionally attach a file) and click **Schedule delivery**.
In **Scheduled**, use **Proof of delivery** to capture the driver, handover checklist and signature, and add delivery photos.

body.text: Cards show quick chips for what is on file — **Invoice**, **POP** (proof of payment), a photo count, and the scheduled date. You can also **Print delivery note** from the scheduled stages. If stock has been allocated, a chip shows the unit's readiness (allocated, in PDI, or ready to hand over) and links to the unit.
The stat strip at the top shows active handovers, counts per stage, and total pipeline value.
The action buttons on each card require the **manage deliveries** permission. Without it the board is read-only visibility of vehicles moving to handover.

title: Monthly targets and progress
summary: See this month's goals and live progress across leads, sales value, deliveries and services.

body.text: The **Targets** page shows this month's goals with live progress. Each metric has a progress bar that turns green once you hit the target.
The four metrics

rows: Total value of leads won this month.

body.text: Each card shows the actual figure, and where a target is set, the target and the percentage achieved. If no target has been set for the month, the card notes that.
Setting the targets is owner-only — see the managers' guide. Everyone can view progress.

title: Setting this month's targets
summary: Owners set the monthly goals for leads, sales value, deliveries and services.

body.text: Owners can set the goals that the whole team tracks against on the Targets page. Targets are set per calendar month.

items: Open the **Targets** page.
In **Set this month's targets**, enter a value for each metric — New leads, Sales value (in rand), Deliveries and Services completed.
Click **Save targets**.

body.text: Leave a metric blank to have no target for it that month; its card will simply show the running actual with no percentage.

title: Reading the sales forecast
summary: View weighted, commit and best-case pipeline for a period, filtered by pipeline, team and owner.

body.text: The **Sales forecast** projects open pipeline for a month. Access requires the *view forecast* permission, and what you see is scoped to the leads, teams and owners you're allowed to view.
Filtering
Use the filter bar to choose the **Period** (month), **Pipeline**, **Team** and **Owner**, then click **Apply**. The KPI cards and table update to match.
The KPI cards

rows: Value adjusted by each deal's probability.

body.text: The table lists each open lead with its pipeline and stage, owner and team, expected close date, forecast category, probability, value, and weighted value (value × probability).

title: Adjusting forecast deals and capturing snapshots
summary: Managers set per-deal probability, category and close date, and snapshot the forecast for the record.

body.text: With the *manage forecast* permission you can tune the forecast inputs for each deal and capture point-in-time snapshots. These controls are hidden for users who can only view.
Editing a deal

items: In the forecast table, open the **Edit** control on a lead's row.
Set the **probability** (0–100).
Choose a **forecast category**: Pipeline, Best case, Commit or Omitted.
Set the **expected close date** and, optionally, an **estimated cost**.
If you can assign leads, set the **team**. Save.

body.text: The forecast category determines which KPI a deal rolls into — for example, deals marked *Commit* count toward the Commit total, and *Omitted* deals are excluded.
Capturing a snapshot

Click **Capture snapshot** to freeze the current forecast (for the selected period, pipeline, team and owner). Recent snapshots are listed at the bottom of the page showing open value, weighted value, deal count and when they were captured.

title: Getting a quote signed online
summary: Countersign for Denago, then send the customer a secure link so they sign on their phone and accept the quote.

body.text: A quote can be signed online from the **Online signature** card on its record. Signing a quote both accepts it and, if it's linked to a lead, wins the lead — no printing needed.
The two-step quote flow

items: **Step 1 — Denago countersigns.** Use the signature pad on the quote to countersign for the dealership (you can reuse a saved signature).
Optionally pick a **signing workflow** — the built-in flow (Denago countersigns, then the customer) or a custom approval chain.
Click **Send for signing**.
**Step 2 — the customer signs.** Copy the secure link and send it, or resend from the card. The customer reviews and signs on their phone.

body.text: While a request is active
The card shows each recipient's status (sent, viewed, signed) with a copyable link. You can **Resend link**, **Manage in hub**, or **Void request** to stop the link working and start over.
While a signing request is active the quote is **locked for editing**. Void the request to make changes, then send a fresh one.
An expired quote can't be sent for signing — issue an updated quote first. Once signed, the sealed PDF is filed in the customer's documents with a SHA-256 tamper-evidence hash.

title: Tracking signatures in the hub
summary: Monitor every signing request, chase recipients, run approvals, and read the full audit trail.

body.text: The **Signatures** hub is the owner-only command centre for every signing request. It shows all requests with progress, plus headline stats: total, awaiting, completed, completion rate and median time to complete.
Request status and signers

Each request shows how many signers have signed, whether it runs **sequential** or **parallel**, and a per-signer state (signed, opened but not signed, sent but not opened, or not sent) with exact dates. In a sequential run the signer you're waiting on is flagged as *up next*. Recipients can be **signers**, **approvers** or **viewers**.
Working a request

items: **Send for signing / Resend** — dispatch to recipients.
**Void** — recipients can no longer sign; the audit record is kept.
**Remind** a specific recipient, or update their **email / phone** for delivery.
**Sign in person** — open the signing surface on your device and hand it to the recipient.
Open the **Unsigned PDF** or, once complete, the **Signed PDF**.

body.text: Approvals
When a workflow includes approval steps, **Pending approvals** appears at the top of the hub. Approve a step, or reject it with a reason.
The audit trail logs every event — sent, viewed, signed, reminded, voided — with the actor, channel, IP and time. A failed email or WhatsApp is flagged so it doesn't look like a successful send.

title: Building custom signing workflows
summary: Owners design node-based approval and signing chains that can be applied when sending a quote.

body.text: Signing workflows let owners design a custom chain of signers and approvers, instead of using the built-in flow. They're built in a visual, node-based editor and managed under **Settings → Signing workflows**.
Editing a workflow

items: Open a workflow to launch the visual builder.
Lay out the signer and approver nodes and assign staff where needed.
Name and save the workflow. Use **Delete workflow** to remove one.

body.text: Once saved, a workflow appears in the **Signing workflow** dropdown on a quote's Online signature card, so you can route that quote through the custom chain when you send it for signing.
Building and editing signing workflows is owner-only.

title: Tracking and rewarding referrals
summary: Follow customer introductions from referral code to won deal, and redeem the reward when it's earned.

body.text: The **Referrals** page tracks customer introductions from a shared referral code through to a won deal and reward redemption. Every customer has one permanent, unique **referral code** on their contact record (shown as DGO-XXXX).
How a referral progresses

rows: Introduction made — awaiting a won deal.
The referred deal was won — the reward is now owed.

body.text: When a new lead is captured with a customer's code, a referral is linked to that referrer. When the deal is won, the referral automatically becomes **fee due**. Self-referrals and unknown codes are ignored, so lead capture never fails on a typo.
Redeeming a reward

items: Find the referral marked **fee due**.
In the **Reward provided** field, note what was given (for example, 'R1,000 voucher').
Click **Mark reward redeemed**.

body.text: The three KPI cards summarise rewards due, introductions in progress, and rewards already redeemed. Redeeming a reward requires the *manage referrals* permission.
